subsystems.name: Light source
subsystems.role: supplies the laser light the chip carries and modulates.
parts: edge or grating coupling into the chip

subsystems.name: Waveguides and passive optics
subsystems.role: guide and split light on-chip with very low loss.
parts: ring resonators and arrayed waveguide gratings

subsystems.name: Modulators
subsystems.role: imprint an electrical data signal onto the light.
parts: doping and electrodes for the free-carrier effect

subsystems.name: Photodetectors
subsystems.role: convert incoming light back into an electrical signal.

subsystems.name: Packaging and fibre attach
subsystems.role: gets light in and out of the chip and keeps it thermally stable.

subsystems.name: Electronic control
subsystems.role: drives, amplifies and stabilises the photonic circuits.

buildSteps.title: Design and tape-out
buildSteps.detail: Photonic components are laid out alongside control electronics using a foundry process design kit, with optical simulation to set waveguide widths and ring radii.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the waveguides
buildSteps.detail: The circuit is patterned on a silicon-on-insulator wafer using deep-ultraviolet lithography; etching leaves silicon ridges roughly 200–500 nm across that confine light at near-infrared wavelengths around 1310 and 1550 nm.

buildSteps.title: Dope and metallise
buildSteps.detail: Regions of the silicon are doped to form diodes and heaters, then metal layers are deposited for electrodes and wiring.

buildSteps.title: Grow the detectors
buildSteps.detail: Germanium is epitaxially grown on selected areas and processed into photodiodes, because silicon itself is transparent at telecom wavelengths.

buildSteps.title: Add the lasers
buildSteps.detail: Indium phosphide laser dies are flip-chip bonded or wafer-bonded onto the silicon, since silicon cannot emit light efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Dice and package
buildSteps.detail: The wafer is diced; fibres are actively aligned to couplers and fixed in place, and the chip is assembled with driver and amplifier dies into a module.

buildSteps.title: Test and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Optical probe stations check every circuit on the wafer; packaged modules are tuned for wavelength, biased for best modulation efficiency and burned in.

buildSteps.title: Build the system
buildSteps.detail: Modules become pluggable transceivers or are mounted next to switch and accelerator chips as co-packaged optics.

prerequisites.why: silicon photonics can only scale if it reuses existing wafer fabs and their lithography.
lasers must be bonded or grown on silicon, and this is still the hardest step to make high-yield.
getting fibres aligned to many parallel channels cheaply is often the limiting cost.
designers need one workflow that simulates light and electrons together.
photonic chips are only useful where fibre already reaches.

pathway.milestone: silicon photonics inside pluggable 400 and 800 Gbit/s data-centre transceivers
pathway.unlocks: cheap, high-volume optical links between racks.

pathway.milestone: co-packaged optics, with the photonic engine beside the switch chip instead of in a pluggable module
pathway.unlocks: lower power per bit and far more bandwidth per switch.

pathway.milestone: optical input/output between chips within a system
pathway.unlocks: accelerators linked by light without leaving the board.

pathway.milestone: photonic circuits that compute, not just transmit
pathway.unlocks: matrix multiplication or signal processing at the speed of light, if on-chip memory and control catch up.
